subject: Proposal: SCCs + UK IDTA approach and DocuSign execution plan
messages:
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acmehealth.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 17:12:00 +0000
Subject: Acme Health DPA: initial redlines and question on transfers

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the call this morning. We reviewed the DPA and attached a redline (AcmeHealth_DPA_Redline_v3.docx). Main asks from our side:

- Include Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) as the primary transfer mechanism for EU data.
- Add UK IDTA addendum language for UK data flows.
- Clarify whether Redwood will accept the UK Addendum in the DocuSign flow or if a separate signed addendum is required.
- Confirm subprocessors; we flagged a few named vendors in the list provided.

Can you confirm Redwood's approach to the transfer impact assessment (TIA) and the draft supplementary measures you propose? Also please send the most current subprocessors export.

Best,
Jane
Legal Operations
Acme Health

[Attachment: AcmeHealth_DPA_Redline_v3.docx]

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 09:01:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Acme Health DPA: initial redlines and question on transfers

Team — forwarding Acme's redline and asks. Quick summary of what's new vs. usual: SCCs + explicit UK IDTA requested, plus a list of named subprocessors they want to vet (see attached CSV we pulled).

Recommended approach (high level):
- Accept SCCs as the default for EU transfers and append Redwood's standard Supplementary Measures PDF (attached) outlining technical and contractual controls.
- For UK: offer the IDTA addendum as an integrated DocuSign exhibit so they don't need a separate paper signing step. That should be legal-approved but requires a quick redline to our standard IDTA text.
- Subprocessors: propose a 10-business-day notice window to review critical subprocessors and a rollback/mitigation commitment for any showstoppers.

Sooj, can you draft the minimal redline for the IDTA addendum that we can present back? Neha, can you prepare a short transfer impact memo and the supplementary measures doc for Acme's security team? Kar, please flag any pricing/contract implications if they insist on named-subprocessor approvals.

I think we can keep this to a single DocuSign envelope with DPA + SCCs + UK addendum as exhibits to avoid multiple signature events. Leaning to agree to their SCC ask but we should keep the supplementary measures explicit (see RWD_SCCs_Supplementary_Measures_20260224.pdf).

Thanks — Rishi
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: subprocessors_current_list_20260220.csv]

From: soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 14:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Acme Health DPA: initial redlines and question on transfers

I've drafted an IDTA addendum redline that mirrors our standard UK addendum but with two clarifications Acme asked for:

1) Explicit confirmation that SCCs are incorporated by reference into the DPA, and that the UK Addendum operates as the equivalent for UK transfers.
2) Language on onward transfers: we keep the right to engage subprocessors listed in our registry, with notice and a 10-business-day review window for critical data processors (their "named" vendors can be escalated).

I've attached both the redline and a short Transfer Impact Memo summarizing our assessment of the legal landscape and the supplementary measures we propose. Key points for negotiation:
- We can't accept per-subprocessor vetting that allows them to unilaterally block commonly used cloud infra vendors without a contractual workaround.
- Offer: an SLA-level mitigation commitment + temporary suspension rights in extreme cases.

If we agree, I suggest we send back a single consolidated redline (DPA + SCCs + UK Addendum) and propose a call with Acme legal next Wednesday. I'll also prepare a DocuSign-ready exhibit layout.

Soojin Lee
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: IDTA_addendum_redline_20260224.docx, Transfer_Impact_Memo_20260224.pdf]

Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 09:20:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Proposal: SCCs + UK IDTA approach and DocuSign execution plan

Rishi — thank you and please thank your legal team for the quick turnaround. We reviewed Soojin's redline and the transfer memo. A couple of follow-ups from Acme Security:

- Supplementary measures: they want a short appendix listing encryption-at-rest details, key management, and retention windows. The memo you sent covers those but they'd like it pulled into the DocuSign exhibit.
- Subprocessors: they want one named vendor (CloudCache Analytics) removed unless Redwood can provide a data segregation description.
- DocuSign: procurement prefers a single-envelope flow with DPA + SCCs + UK Addendum attached, signed by the Acme legal signatory and procurement. Can Redwood produce a DocuSign envelope link for review before sending to sign?

We can do a call on Wednesday 11:00 GMT (their time) to walk through final redlines if that helps.

Regards,
Jane
Legal Operations
Acme Health
